about: ShroudForge mod packages (mod.json + extended.mod.json): how a setting reads (type, label, control, when it applies, enabledWhen) and how the switch and the settings are written (only the value changes, the rest of the file stays byte-identical). Run by crates/kiln-manage/tests/shroudforge_fixtures.rs (the launcher) and managed/tests/Kiln.Ui.Tests/ShroudForgeTests.cs (the in-game Mods page); ShroudForge's own rules: modules/modloader/read_mod_settings.rs, validate_mod_settings.rs and mod-runtime/ingame/refresh_runtime_configuration.rs in the fork. Edits run in order; a refused edit leaves the file as it was. A case with "refused": true is one ShroudForge refuses: both readers refuse it and nothing is written. "extendedLatin1" gives the file one byte per character (not UTF-8). "limits.fileBytes" is the largest extended.mod.json both readers take. "modText" supplies exact mod.json bytes instead of serializing "mod". "errorContains" checks both the refusal reason and that the message names ShroudForge. "sfRefused": true marks only the earlier-Kiln fractional recovery exception: SF refuses the input, Kiln exposes repair, and SF must accept every successful written output.

cases.name: runtime-mod
cases.about: sf-survival's shape: a runtime mod, settings without applyAt (ShroudForge's default: restart), one group

cases.name: patch-mod
cases.about: sf-crafting-essentials' shape: startup asset changes plus a runtime part; only settings declared live apply live, the switch at the next start

cases.name: one-line-file
cases.about: ShroudForge accepts this one-line package: shorthand settings, fractional values, escaped Unicode text and matching integer enabledWhen operands. Switch and value edits preserve the surrounding bytes.

cases.name: lists-and-bool-options
cases.about: a list setting with options (a multiselect when no control is given) and a yes/no setting shown as options

cases.name: switch-added-to-a-file-without-one
cases.about: ShroudForge refuses an existing extension without its required enabled boolean. Neither switch writes (including an already-off request) nor setting edits silently make an invalid package look healthy.

cases.name: crlf-and-bom
cases.about: ShroudForge's plain serde_json package reader refuses this byte order mark; both Kiln readers refuse it and leave every byte unchanged.

cases.name: legacy-eml-package
cases.about: no extended.mod.json: the first switch writes the file ShroudForge's ensure_eml_extension would

cases.name: jsonc-comments-and-typed-options
cases.about: ShroudForge's plain serde_json package reader refuses this commented JSON; both Kiln readers refuse it and leave every byte unchanged.

cases.name: conditional-chains
cases.about: ShroudForge accepts this acyclic enabledWhen chain with matching integer operands. Changing its root disables both descendants; refused cycles and missing controllers have separate cases.

cases.name: fractional-list
cases.about: a list typed by a fractional first member: whole members are written with a fraction (1.0), or ShroudForge would type the list by an integer first member and refuse the fractional option keys

cases.name: damaged-fractional-values-are-repaired
cases.about: what an earlier Kiln wrote for a fractional setting (a whole first member or value without its fraction): ShroudForge refuses the mod ("invalid option": an integer first member, fractional option keys). It is read as the fractional setting it was, listed under "repair", and the next write (here the switch) puts the fraction back. A later whole member ([2.5, 1]) is what ShroudForge accepts and stays as it is; an integer setting with whole option keys stays an integer setting Explicit recovery exception: SF refuses the input, not the repaired output; retaining this path avoids stranding settings damaged by an earlier Kiln.

cases.name: damaged-values-are-repaired-by-a-settings-write
cases.about: the repair of damaged-fractional-values-are-repaired through a change of another setting (not the switch): the fraction comes back on every damaged setting Explicit recovery exception: SF refuses the input, not the repaired output; retaining this path avoids stranding settings damaged by an earlier Kiln.

cases.name: comment-ends-at-a-lone-cr

cases.name: cr-only-line-ends
cases.about: ShroudForge's plain serde_json package reader refuses this commented JSON; both Kiln readers refuse it and leave every byte unchanged.

cases.name: empty-options-are-refused
cases.about: ShroudForge's schema requires options to name at least one choice (minProperties 1): "options": {} refuses the mod

cases.name: empty-options-on-a-list-are-refused
cases.about: the same for a list (ShroudForge: minProperties 1, and a list must declare options)

cases.name: negative-zero-is-fractional
cases.about: ShroudForge's serde_json reads -0 as a float: a fractional setting, whose option keys are read as fractions (0 is 0.0) and whose whole values keep a fraction

cases.name: numbers-are-written-as-shroudforge-writes-them
cases.about: a fractional setting gets serde_json's form of the double (shortest digits; a fraction or an exponent always, so ShroudForge keeps the type); an integer setting gets an integer

cases.name: duplicate-keys-last-one-counts
cases.about: ShroudForge's serde_json keeps the last of a repeated key, in the place of the first

cases.name: length-limits-are-whole-number-tokens
cases.about: ShroudForge reads minLength/maxLength with as_u64: 4.0 is no limit, 1 is

cases.name: option-keys-as-shroudforge-reads-them
cases.about: ShroudForge's option keys: a yes/no key is true only as "true"; numbers as Rust's str::parse reads them; a fractional key that is not a finite number is an option without a value

cases.name: a-choice-without-a-value-cannot-come-first
cases.about: a fractional key that is not a finite double is a choice without a value (null). As the first member it would make ShroudForge read the list as text and refuse the mod, so that edit is refused; after another member ShroudForge accepts it

cases.name: lone-surrogate-is-refused
cases.about: ShroudForge's serde_json refuses a lone surrogate escape

cases.name: number-out-of-range-is-refused
cases.about: ShroudForge's serde_json refuses a number beyond a double

cases.name: number-out-of-range-in-metadata-is-refused
cases.about: anywhere in the file

cases.name: enabledWhen-null-is-refused
cases.about: ShroudForge reads enabledWhen as a condition object; null is not one

cases.name: option-labels-must-be-text
cases.about: ShroudForge refuses an option label that is not a string

cases.name: option-key-with-spaces-is-refused
cases.about: Rust's str::parse (ShroudForge) does not take spaces around a number

cases.name: typed-lists-cannot-lose-their-element-type
cases.about: ShroudForge types options by the first list member (an empty list uses text). Clearing a numeric or boolean list would turn its choices into strings on the next read, so refuse that edit; a text list may be cleared.

cases.name: legacy-manifest-enabled-is-not-the-sf-switch
cases.about: ShroudForge ignores a legacy mod.json enabled member: without an extension the mod stays disabled until enabled is persisted in extended.mod.json.

cases.name: extension-must-be-an-object
cases.about: ShroudForge refuses an extension that is not an object; the launcher must not turn it into an apparently disabled package with no settings.

cases.name: settings-cannot-be-an-array
cases.about: A present settings member must be an object, even an empty array is not an empty set of settings.

cases.name: settings-cannot-be-null
cases.about: An absent settings member means no settings; an explicit null is refused by ShroudForge.

cases.name: invalid-utf8-is-refused
cases.about: a Latin-1 byte (not UTF-8): ShroudForge's serde_json refuses the file, and a lossy read would write U+FFFD back

cases.name: crlf-line-ends
cases.about: ShroudForge accepts strict JSON with these line endings; writes preserve all layout outside the requested values.

cases.name: cr-only-layout

cases.name: typed-options-and-unicode-text
cases.about: ShroudForge accepts these typed options and Unicode text in strict JSON. Numeric option keys keep their declared spelling; whole fractional choices are written with a fraction.
